strings.d1.s0.name: War Remnants Museum
strings.d1.s0.tips: A museum of the Vietnam War: heavy but important. Cooler in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Independence Palace
strings.d1.s1.tips: The palace tanks crashed into in 1975, with 1960s architecture and a bunker.
strings.d1.s2.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Saigon
strings.d1.s2.tips: The French cathedral (under restoration), with the Central Post Office opposite.
strings.d1.s3.name: Pho Hoa Pasteur
strings.d1.s3.tips: A classic spot serving pho since 1968, on Pasteur Street.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ben Thanh Market
strings.d1.s4.tips: The city's iconic market: coffee, dried mango, and haggling is a must.
strings.d1.b0.name: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa
strings.d1.b0.tips: Saigon's most famous banh mi, with 10 kinds of meat and a long queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Saigon Central Post Office
strings.d1.b1.tips: A post office designed by Eiffel; step inside to see it.
strings.d2.s0.name: Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Duoc
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~500,000 VND, or bus number 13); a 200 km tunnel network. Ben Duoc is less touristy, with 20-100 m crawls.
strings.d2.s1.name: Cu Chi Tapioca Tasting
strings.d2.s1.tips: War-era tapioca and tea at the tunnel exit; included in the tour.
strings.d2.s2.name: Cu Chi Local Eatery
strings.d2.s2.tips: Eat com tam (broken rice) on the way back.
strings.d2.s3.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
strings.d2.s3.tips: Saigon's most atmospheric temple, with a turtle pond and incense.
strings.d2.s4.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
strings.d2.s4.tips: A pedestrian boulevard in front of the City Hall; cafes in the Cafe Apartment building (42 Nguyen Hue).
strings.d2.b0.name: Cafe Apartment Saigon
strings.d2.b0.tips: A 9-storey apartment block full of cafes; balcony views.
strings.d2.b1.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: City history; an alternative to the pagoda.
strings.d3.s0.name: Binh Tay Market
strings.d3.s0.tips: Cho Lon's wholesale market; lively in the morning, with street breakfast.
strings.d3.s1.name: Thien Hau Temple
strings.d3.s1.tips: A temple to the sea goddess, with hanging spiral incense.
strings.d3.s2.name: Cho Lon Street Food Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: Hu tieu (Cho Lon noodles) and dim sum on Ha Ton Quyen street.
strings.d3.s3.name: Cha Tam Church
strings.d3.s3.tips: The church where Diem was captured, in Cho Lon.
strings.d3.s4.name: Bui Vien Walking Street
strings.d3.s4.tips: The backpacker street: plastic stools, beer and noise.
strings.d3.b0.name: Com Tam Ba Ghien
strings.d3.b0.tips: The city's most famous com tam, in Phu Nhuan.
strings.d3.b1.name: Saigon Opera House
strings.d3.b1.tips: The A O Show bamboo circus; an alternative to Bui Vien.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tan Dinh Church
strings.d4.s0.tips: A pink-painted cathedral, ideal for photos.
strings.d4.s1.name: Tan Dinh Market
strings.d4.s1.tips: A local market; banh cuon for breakfast.
strings.d4.s2.name: Cong Caphe
strings.d4.s2.tips: Coconut coffee at Cong Caphe, plus egg coffee.
strings.d4.s3.name: Turtle Lake
strings.d4.s3.tips: The Turtle Lake roundabout: young crowds and street snacks.
strings.d4.s4.name: Secret Garden Restaurant Saigon
strings.d4.s4.tips: Vietnamese home cooking in a rooftop garden, in District 1.
strings.d4.b0.name: Banh Xeo 46A
strings.d4.b0.tips: Vietnamese savoury pancakes on Dinh Cong Trang.
strings.d4.b1.name: Fine Arts Museum Saigon
strings.d4.b1.tips: Art in a colonial mansion; an alternative to coffee.
strings.d5.s0.name: Vinh Trang Pagoda
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~600,000 VND, lunch included); giant Buddhas.
strings.d5.s1.name: Mekong River Boat Tour
strings.d5.s1.tips: A boat on the main river, with Unicorn Island and honey and coconut candy workshops.
strings.d5.s2.name: Ben Tre Canoe Tour
strings.d5.s2.tips: A sampan through palm-lined canals; included in the tour.
strings.d5.s3.name: Mekong Island Restaurant
strings.d5.s3.tips: Elephant ear fish and rice paper; included in the tour.
strings.d5.s4.name: Ben Tre Coconut Workshop
strings.d5.b0.name: Cai Be Floating Market
strings.d5.b0.tips: A morning floating market; an alternative to My Tho (early start).
strings.d5.b1.name: My Tho Hu Tieu Restaurant
strings.d5.b1.tips: My Tho noodles; an alternative to the island.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bitexco Saigon Skydeck
strings.d6.s0.tips: Views from the 49th floor; visibility is clear in the morning.
strings.d6.s1.name: Ho Thi Ky Flower Market
strings.d6.s1.tips: A flower market with Cambodian street food, in District 10.
strings.d6.s2.name: Ho Thi Ky Cambodian Noodles
strings.d6.s2.tips: Num banh chok, inside the market.
strings.d6.s3.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
strings.d6.s3.tips: Vietnam's tallest building, in Binh Thanh.
strings.d6.s4.name: Thu Thiem Riverfront
strings.d6.s4.tips: The city skyline at sunset from the new bridge; cafes.
strings.d6.b0.name: Quan Ut Ut Thu Thiem
strings.d6.b1.name: Saigon Waterbus
strings.d6.b1.tips: The river bus from Bach Dang; a cheaper alternative to Landmark.
strings.d7.s0.name: Tao Dan Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: Morning tai chi and birdcage coffee: the city's ritual.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pho Le
strings.d7.s1.tips: Sweet-style pho in District 5; a farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Saigon Square
strings.d7.s3.name: L'Usine Le Loi
strings.d7.s3.tips: A cafe-boutique with coffee and pastries; a farewell stop.
strings.d7.s4.name: Tan Son Nhat Airport Bus 109
strings.d7.s4.tips: 30 minutes to the airport by bus; farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Banh Mi 37 Nguyen Trai
strings.d7.b0.tips: Banh mi with grilled meatballs, from a street cart.
strings.d7.b1.name: Saigon Botanical Garden
strings.d7.b1.tips: A botanical garden and zoo; an alternative to the park.
strings.note0: Grab (motorbike or car) is cheap and safe; a motorbike taxi costs 30,000-60,000 VND. Metro Line 1 (Ben Thanh-Suoi Tien) is open.
strings.note1: June to September is the rainy season: afternoon downpours are common, so sightsee in the morning and take an umbrella. Expect 32°C and humidity.
strings.note2: Pho costs 60-90,000 VND, banh mi 30-60,000, coffee 30-60,000. Street stools are safe, and the ice is factory-made.
strings.note3: For Cu Chi and the Mekong, a tour (hotel pickup included) is the most practical option. The Ben Duoc tunnels are quieter than Ben Dinh.
strings.note4: Cross the road at a steady pace (motorbikes will swerve around you). To avoid bag snatchers, don't hold your phone in your hand on the street.
strings.note5: Tipping is not expected; haggle 30-50% off at markets.
